subject: Post-call: Budget range & token volume validation
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>

Subject: Post-call: Budget range & token volume validation

Hi Jessica 

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and a couple asks so we can align pricing and next steps: 

Call recap:
- Use case: customer support summarization + routing + embeddings for search
- Expected traffic: mainly US, some EU (regional redundancy later)
- Key success metric: 95th percentile latency < 300ms for chat flows

Pricing/volume asks (please confirm):
1) Monthly token volume band: on the call we discussed a rough band of 25M-100M tokens/mo. Can you confirm the likely range for the first 6 months (conservative / expected / optimistic)?
2) Target unit economics: you mentioned target is roughly $900/1M tokens - can you confirm whether that is a firm procurement target or flexible with committed discounts?
3) Procurement thresholds: can you confirm the internal approval cutoffs we should plan for (e.g., up to $50k product/finance sign-off, >$50k requires procurement/legal, >$200k needs VP approval)?

Attachments: I'm including the usage projection workbook we discussed (Acme-usage-projections.xlsx) - feel free to update any numbers and re-share.

Next steps I suggest:
- You confirm the 3-month and 6-month token bands and procurement limits
- If the 30-60M range looks right, I'll share a 60-day MAP + committed-tier pricing that targets $/1M tokens in the $800-$950 band with graduated discounts for committed spend

If helpful, I can loop in Rishi from pricing to run an initial committed vs PAYG P&L for your finance team.

Thanks - talk soon.


Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Jessica Alvarez <jessica@acmepayments.com>

Subject: Re: Post-call: Budget range & token volume validation

Hi Marissa 

Thanks for the clear recap. A few quick answers below and I've attached our current expected-usage dump for the first two quarters.

1) Token volume band (conservative / expected / optimistic):
- Conservative: ~30M tokens/mo
- Expected: ~45-60M tokens/mo
- Optimistic: 90-120M tokens/mo (if we roll out to N. America + EU in Q4)

2) Target unit economics:
- Our procurement target is roughly $900/1M tokens as a benchmark; finance is open to committed discounts if there's visibility on 6-12 month volumes 

3) Procurement thresholds (US corporate):
- <= $75k: product/finance approval (no PO required)
- > $75k and <= $200k: procurement + legal review; typical turnaround 2-3 weeks
- > $200k: VP approval required and standard RFP/IT security questionnaire

What would help next is a 3-tier proposal: DEV (low volume, PAYG), PROD (committed tier for expected band), ENTERPRISE (dedicated/reserved capacity + SLA). If you can share a sample committed-tier P&L and an indicative $/1M for each tier that'd be great.

Attachment: Acme-expected-usage.csv

Thanks 
Jessica Alvarez
Head of Product Ops | Acme Payments
jessica@acmepayments.com
(212) 555-0148

Hi Jessica 

Appreciate the clarification - that band (30-60M expected) is very actionable. Below is an initial, high-level unit economics layout we can use to build the 3-tier proposal you requested. This is intentionally simple so procurement/finance can model quickly; we'll follow with a spreadsheet-backed MAP.

Indicative pricing (USD per 1M tokens) - public / illustrative:
- DEV (PAYG, no commit): $1,100 / 1M tokens
- PROD (committed tier, 6-12 month): $850 / 1M tokens for 30-60M commit band; escalators for 60-100M to $800 / 1M
- ENTERPRISE (reserved/dedicated): contact us for reserved pricing; typically equivalent to $700-$780 / 1M tokens with SLA & dedicated capacity depending on NKs/throughput

Example math for expected band (45-60M tokens/mo):
- PAYG: 50M * $1,100/1M = $55,000/mo (~$660k/yr)
- Committed (PROD) at $850/1M: 50M * $850 = $42,500/mo (~$510k/yr) - ~23% savings vs PAYG

Procurement alignment notes:
- We can structure a 6-month committed contract with a monthly true-up and finance-friendly invoicing to keep you below immediate VP escalation thresholds; e.g., 6-month PO at estimated $255k would sit in the $200k-$300k corridor so we should plan procurement/legal engagement early.

Next steps I propose:
1) I'll share a tightened 3-tier PDF and a MAP (attached: Redwood-pricing-tier-sample.pdf) by EOD today
2) If the PROD committed example looks reasonable, let's schedule a 30-min procurement sync next week to walk PO timing and security questionnaire
3) If you confirm the 6-month projection, I'll generate a draft contract and route to DocuSign (link below)

HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/1234567
DocuSign (sample): https://www.docusign.com/contract/ABCD-1234

Thanks - looping Rishi to help with committed-tier P&L and any custom pricing asks.

Best,
